name: Goa
short_description: Sun-kissed Arabian shores, bohemian flea markets, Portuguese villas & legendary sunset parties.
long_story: Goa is an iconic kaleidoscope of sun, sea, and Indo-Portuguese soul. From the tranquil fishing hamlets of South Goa with their secluded palm-fringed sands to the pulsating beach shacks and night markets of the North, it offers an escape for every tempo of travel. Cycle through Latin Quarters in Fontainhas, feast on spicy fish curry rice, or watch the sky turn tangerine over Vagator.
rainfall_information: Heavy tropical monsoon from June to September; dry and sunny from October to May.
crowd_information: High peak during December–January; calm and relaxed from July to September.
culture: A harmonious blend of Konkani traditions and 450 years of Portuguese architecture and lifestyle.
people: Known for 'susegad' — a relaxed, contented, and warm outlook on life.
clothing: Light breathable cottons, beachwear, comfortable sandals, sunglasses & hats.
food: Goan Fish Curry, Prawn Balchão, Bebinca, Poi bread, Xacuti, Pork Vindaloo, Feni.
must_try_foods: Goan Prawn Curry Thali
Pork/Chicken Vindaloo
Warm Bebinca with vanilla scoop
Fresh Kokum Sharbat
history: Ruled by Kadamba dynasty, Adil Shahi sultans, and Portuguese colonizers from 1510 until liberation in 1961.
heritage_story: Fontainhas still retains vibrant pastel homes, oyster-shell window panes, and charming old balconies.
travel_tips: Rent a two-wheeler or self-drive car for effortless exploration.
Carry sunscreen and drink tender coconut water frequently.
North Goa is vibrant & happening; South Goa is quiet, serene & boutique.
local_etiquette: Respect sacred dress codes when visiting churches and temples.
Avoid littering plastic on the beaches; keep Goa pristine.
Always ask fishermen before snapping close-up portraits.

faq.q: Is Goa safe for solo female travellers?
faq.a: Yes, Goa is widely regarded as one of the safest tourist destinations in India.

faq.q: What is the best way to get around Goa?
faq.a: Renting a scooter or self-drive car offers the maximum flexibility.

name: Manali & Himachal
short_description: Snow-capped peaks, roaring Beas river, pine forests, hipster cafes & gateway to high mountain passes.
long_story: Nestled in the breathtaking Beas River valley, Manali blends fairy-tale pine groves with high-octane Himalayan thrill. Explore rustic wooden temples in Old Manali, cross through the engineering marvel of Atal Tunnel to reach barren Sissu, or curl up with hot ginger lemon honey tea in a bohemian cedar cafe.
best_time_to_visit: March to June (Summer) & October to February (Snow)
rainfall_information: Monsoon rains in July-August; heavy snowfall between late December and February.
crowd_information: High during May-June and Christmas-New Year week.
culture: Dev Bhoomi folklore, Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, and wood-and-stone Kath Kuni architecture.
people: Generous and welcoming mountain locals with deep reverence for nature and local deities.
clothing: Thermal innerwear, fleece, heavy down jacket in winter; light jacket for summer evenings.
food: Siddu with ghee, Trout fish, Thukpa, Momos, Babru, Kullu Dham.
must_try_foods: Steaming hot Siddu with walnut chutney
Fresh Tirthan Valley grilled trout
Tibetan Butter Tea & Thukpa
history: Named after the sage Manu, believed to have recreated human life here after the great deluge.
heritage_story: Hadimba Temple, built in 1553 inside Dhungri Van Vihar, stands completely carved of cedar wood.
travel_tips: Book your Rohtang Pass permit well in advance during summer months.
Acclimatize properly if heading higher into Spiti or Leh from Manali.
Carry good trekking shoes with anti-slip grip.
local_etiquette: Do not touch religious deities or temple sanctums unless invited.
Respect mountain serenity; avoid loud music on nature trails.

map_markers.name: Hadimba Temple
map_markers.desc: Ancient wooden temple amid cedar woods

map_markers.name: Solang Valley
map_markers.desc: Hub for paragliding, zorbing & winter skiing

map_markers.desc: World's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet

map_markers.name: Jogini Waterfalls
map_markers.desc: Cascading mountain waterfall accessible via scenic hike

faq.q: When does it snow in Manali?
faq.a: Snowfall typically begins around mid-to-late December and continues through February.

name: Kashmir
short_description: Paradise on Earth: Dal Lake shikaras, cedar-rimmed Gulmarg meadows & saffron valleys.
long_story: Celebrated by poets for centuries, Kashmir is a dream painted in willow trees, chinars, and snow-draped peaks. Wake up to misty mornings on a cedar-carved houseboat on Dal Lake, ride the world's highest gondola over powdery slopes in Gulmarg, and stroll through the meadows of Pahalgam where shepherd flutes echo against pine hills.
best_time_to_visit: March to October (Greenery & Flowers) / Dec to Feb (Snow)
rainfall_information: Crisp dry summers; snow in winters from late December to February.
crowd_information: Peak during Tulip Festival (April) and Summer holidays (May-June).
culture: Rich Sufi traditions, Pashmina craftsmanship, paper mache artistry, and hospitality.
people: Known for warmth, offering Kahwa tea to visitors with deep graciousness.
clothing: Modest layers; warm thermals and heavy woolens during autumn and winter.
food: Rogan Josh, Gushtaba, Yakhni, Dum Aloo, Nadru Yakhni, Kashmiri Pulao, Kahwa.
must_try_foods: Authentic 7-course Wazwan feast
Kashmiri Noon Chai with freshly baked Lavasa
Saffron Kahwa with crushed almonds
history: Historical crossroads of Buddhist, Hindu, and Islamic philosophy along the Silk Road.
heritage_story: Houseboats on Dal Lake were first conceived by the British when local kings forbade foreigners from owning land.
travel_tips: Pre-book Gulmarg Gondola tickets Phase 1 & 2 weeks in advance.
Spend at least one night aboard a heritage Dal Lake or Nigeen Lake houseboat.
Bargain politely in artisan handicraft showrooms.
local_etiquette: Dress modestly when visiting Jamia Masjid and Hazratbal Shrine.
top_attractions: Betaab Valley & Aru Valley in Pahalgam

map_markers.name: Dal Lake
map_markers.desc: Jewel of Srinagar featuring shikara rides and floating markets

map_markers.name: Gulmarg Gondola
map_markers.desc: One of the highest cable cars in the world reaching 13,780 feet

map_markers.name: Betaab Valley
map_markers.desc: Verdant valley surrounded by snow-clad mountains in Pahalgam

faq.q: Is Kashmir safe for family tourists?
faq.a: Yes, millions of families and couples visit Jammu & Kashmir every year with standard tourist infrastructure.

name: Kerala
short_description: God's Own Country: tranquil emerald backwaters, rolling Munnar tea hills & Ayurvedic bliss.
long_story: From the spice-scented mountain mists of Munnar to the languid palms of the Alleppey backwaters, Kerala unfolds at a serene, poetic rhythm. Cruise aboard a converted Kettuvallam houseboat, breathe in crisp tea estate air, and experience ancient healing through authentic Ayurvedic therapies.

monthly_weather.verdict: Onam festival & Nehru Trophy Snake Boat races

rainfall_information: Southwest monsoon (June-August) brings nourishing rain; dry season from November to April.
crowd_information: High during December-January and August (Onam boat races).
culture: Kathakali dance-drama, Kalaripayattu martial art, Ayurvedic wellness, and spice trade legacy.
people: High literacy, progressive and gentle demeanor with deep community bonds.
clothing: Breathable cottons, linen shirts, sunhats, and light wrap for evenings in Munnar hills.
food: Appam with vegetable stew, Malabar Parotta with chicken roast, Karimeen Pollichathu, Payasam.
must_try_foods: Pearl Spot fish baked in banana leaf (Karimeen Pollichathu)
Appam with rich coconut milk stew
Traditional Kerala Sadya on banana leaf
history: Ancient maritime center traded with Phoenicians, Romans, and Arabs for cinnamon and black pepper.
heritage_story: Fort Kochi retains Chinese fishing nets, Jewish synagogues, and Dutch palaces side by side.
travel_tips: Combine 2 nights in Munnar hills with 1 night on an Alleppey houseboat.
Taste fresh spice farm infusions in Thekkady.
Wear lifejackets during canoe and bamboo rafting.
local_etiquette: Dhoti/sari may be required for entering certain historic temples in Trivandrum.
Tip houseboat staff respectfully for attentive cooking service.

map_markers.name: Fort Kochi
map_markers.desc: Colonial seaside neighborhood with iconic cantilevered fishing nets

map_markers.name: Munnar Tea Plantations
map_markers.desc: Sprawling rolling emerald tea hills shrouded in mist

map_markers.name: Alleppey Backwaters
map_markers.desc: Serene labyrinth of palm-fringed canals, lagoons and houseboats

photo_spots: Fort Kochi fishing nets against dusk

faq.q: Is food included on Alleppey houseboats?
faq.a: Yes, authentic Kerala meals (lunch, dinner, breakfast) are freshly prepared onboard by your private chef.

name: Rajasthan
short_description: Land of Maharajas: golden Thar dunes, pink palace corridors, lakeside havelis & royal heritage.
long_story: Rajasthan is a regal journey through centuries of chivalry, romance, and artistic splendor. Marvel at the sandstone ramparts of Jaisalmer glowing like gold in the desert sunset, float past the shimmering white palaces of Udaipur's Lake Pichola, and shop for hand-block prints in the pink bazaar corridors of Jaipur.

monthly_weather.verdict: Extreme heat; visit Mount Abu hill station
Monsoon turns Udaipur hills emerald green

rainfall_information: Arid and semi-arid climate with minimal rainfall outside brief monsoon showers in July-August.
crowd_information: Heaviest in November (Pushkar Fair) and December-January.
culture: Rajput valor, vibrant turbans, Ghoomar dance, Kalbelia music, and miniature paintings.
people: Fiercely proud of royal heritage and known for the greeting 'Padharo Mhare Des' (Welcome to our land).
clothing: Modest breathable cottons, sunglasses, sturdy walking footwear for forts, warm jacket for desert nights.
food: Dal Baati Churma, Laal Maas, Ker Sangri, Gatte ki Sabzi, Pyaaz Kachori, Ghevar.
must_try_foods: Ghee-drenched Dal Baati Churma
Fiery Rajput Laal Maas mutton curry
Honeycomb Ghevar dessert from Jaipur
history: Ancient Rajput kingdoms, Mughal alliances, and majestic sovereign princely states.
heritage_story: Amer Fort's Sheesh Mahal was engineered so that a single oil lamp illuminated the entire mirror-inlaid chamber.
travel_tips: Carry water and wear walking shoes as fort complexes are massive.
Stay in at least one converted heritage Haveli for an authentic royal feel.
Plan camel safari at sunset to avoid harsh midday heat.
local_etiquette: Seek permission before photographing village women or artisans.
Remove shoes before entering palaces and temples.
top_attractions: Jaisalmer Golden Fort & Sam Sand Dunes
hidden_gems: Khuri dunes untouched by tourist crowds

faq.q: Can we visit multiple cities in one week?
faq.a: Yes! The classic Golden Triangle + Udaipur route (Jaipur - Jodhpur - Udaipur) is popular for 6–7 day trips.

name: Uttarakhand
short_description: Land of the Gods: Rishikesh yoga & rafting, sacred Kedarnath peaks, Nainital lakes & Mussoorie hills.
long_story: From the swirling Ganga aartis of Haridwar and the adrenaline rapids of Rishikesh to the silent alpine meadows of Chopta and the sacred Kedarnath shrine, Uttarakhand is an exhilarating Himalayan sanctuary.
best_time_to_visit: March to June & September to November

monthly_weather.verdict: Ideal for river rafting in Rishikesh
Peaceful chills, temples close for winter
Winter holiday vibe in Mussoorie & Nainital

rainfall_information: Heavy monsoon from July to mid-August; clear sunny skies in autumn and spring.
crowd_information: Peak during May-June and festive holidays.
culture: Devbhoomi spiritual rituals, yoga ashrams, folk music, and sacred river veneration.
people: Warm-hearted Garhwalis and Kumaonis with profound respect for sacred peaks and pilgrims.
clothing: Layered woolens, quick-dry clothes for rafting, and reliable hiking shoes.
food: Kafli, Chainsoo, Aloo ke Gutke, Jhangora ki Kheer, Singori sweet, Bal Mithai.
must_try_foods: Aloo ke Gutke with spiced pahadi raita
Nutritious Kafli spinach curry
Almora's famous Bal Mithai
history: Ancient sacred corridor traversed by Adi Shankaracharya and spiritual seekers for millennia.
heritage_story: Tungnath stands at 12,073 ft as the highest Shiva temple in the world.
travel_tips: Carry motion sickness tablets for winding mountain roads.
Check weather advisories if planning high-altitude treks like Kedarkantha or Chopta.
Attend the evening Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat in Rishikesh.
local_etiquette: Alcohol and non-vegetarian food are strictly prohibited in holy river towns like Rishikesh and Haridwar.
Maintain silence and cleanliness along pilgrim trails.
hidden_gems: Landour bakehouses and quiet deodar trails

map_markers.desc: Yoga capital of the world and sacred evening Ganga Aarti

faq.q: When is river rafting open in Rishikesh?
faq.a: Rafting is active from mid-September through June, closing only during the peak monsoon season.

name: Ladakh
short_description: The Land of High Passes: lunar valleys, cobalt Pangong waters, Tibetan gompas & starry galaxies.
long_story: A dramatic high-altitude desert framed by snow-glazed peaks, Ladakh is a bucket-list journey for adventure seekers. Cross Khardung La at 17,582 ft, watch the color-shifting waters of Pangong Tso, ride double-humped Bactrian camels across the silver sand dunes of Hunder, and listen to Buddhist monks chanting in clifftop monasteries.

monthly_weather.verdict: Season opens, roads clear of snow

rainfall_information: High altitude rain shadow desert with negligible precipitation; extremely cold winters.
crowd_information: High from June to August during biking and road trip season.
culture: Mahayana Buddhism, ancient prayer wheels, monastery festivals with Cham mask dances.
people: Gentle, resilient mountain people greeting everyone with heartfelt 'Julley!'.
clothing: Thermal inners, windproof jacket, fleece, UV sunglasses, sunscreen SPF 50+, balaclava.
food: Thukpa, Momos, Tingmo bread, Butter tea, Chhurpi (yak cheese), Skyu stew.
must_try_foods: Hearty Skyu root vegetable pasta stew
Hot steamed Tingmo with spicy dip
Apricot jam and juice from Nubra orchards
history: Ancient kingdom at the crossroad of the Silk Route between India, Tibet, and Central Asia.
heritage_story: Thiksey Monastery resembles the Potala Palace of Lhasa, cascading 12 stories up a desert hill.
travel_tips: CRITICAL: Rest and acclimatize for a full 24–48 hours upon landing in Leh.
Obtain Inner Line Permits (ILP) for Nubra Valley, Pangong, and Hanle.
Stay hydrated: drink 3–4 liters of water daily to prevent AMS.
local_etiquette: Always walk clockwise around monasteries, stupas, and mani stones.
Ask permission before photographing monks in prayer.
top_attractions: Magnetic Hill & Sangam of Indus and Zanskar
hidden_gems: Hanle Dark Sky Reserve for stargazing

map_markers.name: Leh Palace
map_markers.desc: 17th-century former royal palace overlooking Leh town

map_markers.name: Pangong Tso
map_markers.desc: Endorheic lake famous for shifting shades of blue

map_markers.name: Khardung La
map_markers.desc: Legendary mountain pass connecting Leh to Nubra Valley

photo_spots: Diskit Maitreya Buddha statue against desert

faq.q: How to handle altitude sickness in Ladakh?
faq.a: Rest the entire first day in Leh, drink plenty of water, avoid alcohol and smoking, and carry Diamox if advised by your physician.

name: Dubai
short_description: Futuristic skyline, golden Arabian desert dunes, mega-malls, luxury yachts & world-record wonders.
long_story: Rising like a glittering metropolis from golden desert sands, Dubai is a masterclass in modern ambition. Stand atop the Burj Khalifa at 828 meters, conquer sweeping desert dunes in a 4x4, cruise the sparkling Dubai Marina aboard a luxury yacht, and immerse yourself in high-tech spectacles from the Museum of the Future to the Dubai Mall fountains.

monthly_weather.verdict: Pleasant beach days and outdoor dining

rainfall_information: Arid desert climate with very minimal rain, mostly concentrated in January-February.
crowd_information: Extremely high during December-January (Shopping Festival & New Year).
culture: Modern cosmopolitan hub rooted in Emirati bedouin traditions and Islamic values.
people: A global melting pot with over 200 nationalities living and working harmoniously.
clothing: Modest casual wear in malls and public spaces; swimwear acceptable at hotel pools and private beaches.
food: Shawarma, Al Machboos, Luqaimat, Hummus & Falafel, Kunafa, Camel milk gelato.
must_try_foods: Warm crispy Luqaimat with date syrup
Slow-cooked spiced Al Machboos rice
Stretching Turkish ice cream & cheesy Kunafa
history: Evolved from an 18th-century pearl-diving fishing village on Dubai Creek into a global aviation and business titan.
heritage_story: Al Fahidi Historical District showcases traditional wind towers (barjeels) that provided natural desert AC.
travel_tips: Use the clean Dubai Metro to travel seamlessly between airport, malls, and marina.
Pre-book Burj Khalifa At The Top sunset slots for unforgettable skyline views.
Carry an international travel card or credit card for hassle-free cashless payments.
local_etiquette: Dress respectfully when visiting public government buildings and mosques.
Public displays of affection should be kept modest.
top_attractions: Desert Safari with Dune Bashing & BBQ
hidden_gems: Ras Al Khor flamingo wildlife sanctuary

map_markers.desc: Architectural masterpiece inscribed with Arabic calligraphy

activities: Dune bashing in the Lahbab desert
Shopping at gold and spice souks

faq.q: Do Indians need a visa for Dubai?
faq.a: Yes, tourist e-visas can be obtained in 2–3 working days, or Indian passport holders with valid US/UK/Schengen visas get visa-on-arrival.

name: Bali
short_description: Island of the Gods: emerald rice terraces, cliffside temples, bohemian beach clubs & spiritual wellness.
long_story: Bali enchants travellers with its unique blend of spiritual serenity, lush volcanic jungles, and pulsating coastal energy. Swing over rice terraces in Ubud, watch Kecak fire dancers chant as the sun dips behind Uluwatu cliff temple, and sip coconuts at world-famous beach clubs in Canggu and Seminyak.

monthly_weather.verdict: Great deals on luxury private pool villas
Dry season arrives, sunny beach weather
Best weather of the year, cool evenings
Kite festival season, sunny and dry
Warm and pleasant before rainy season
Festive season parties in Canggu & Uluwatu

rainfall_information: Tropical monsoon from November to March; sunny dry season with low humidity from April to October.
crowd_information: Peak during July-August and Christmas/New Year.
culture: Balinese Hinduism, daily Canang Sari floral offerings, gamelan music, and temple pageantry.
people: Extraordinarily gentle, artistic, and hospitable locals welcoming travellers with a warm smile.
clothing: Tropical breathable clothes, beachwear, sarong for temple visits (often rented at gates).
food: Nasi Goreng, Mie Goreng, Satay with peanut sauce, Gado Gado, Babi Guling, Pisang Goreng.
must_try_foods: Crispy Balinese Duck (Bebek Betutu)
Indonesian Satay skewers fresh off charcoal
Açai smoothie bowls in trendy Ubud cafes
history: Century-old Hindu-Buddhist kingdoms that developed intricate Subak irrigation cooperative systems.
heritage_story: Tegallalang rice terraces use the UNESCO-inscribed 9th-century Subak water sharing network.
travel_tips: Rent a scooter in Canggu/Ubud only if you are an experienced rider; otherwise use Grab or private drivers.
Take a speedboat day-trip to Nusa Penida to see Kelingking T-Rex beach.
Carry Indonesian Rupiah cash for street warungs and entrance tickets.
local_etiquette: Never step on the small floral Canang Sari offerings placed on pavements and doorsteps.
Wear a sarong and sash whenever entering temple grounds.
top_attractions: Nusa Penida Island (Kelingking Beach & Broken Beach)
hidden_gems: Tibumana & Tukad Cepung hidden cave waterfalls
Amed black sand beach coral reefs

Snorkeling with manta rays at Nusa Penida
Infinity pool club day at Cretya Ubud

faq.q: Do Indians get Visa on Arrival in Bali?
faq.a: Yes, Indian passport holders get an easy Visa on Arrival (e-VOA) for 30 days at Ngurah Rai International Airport.
